Backend: 5/5 pytest tests pass — (1) login for existing agent-created user 'agentfinal_1781535154@test.com' with 'testing123' returns 200 with UserPublic serialized correctly; (2) admin PUT /api/admin/users/{id} on that user returns 200 (no Pydantic 500 from UserPublic parsing '' as int); (3) admin plain_password update -> new-password login works, then password restored; (4) /api/public/agent-my-clients returns timer_duration_hours as None (never ''); (5) full cycle agent-create-user (via /public/agent-create-user with timer_duration_hours omitted) -> /auth/login with created credentials succeeds. Frontend: (a) Access gate + /login as newly agent-created user 'fetest_bug20_1782908617@test.com' / 'TestFE123!' navigates to /wallet with correct email and username displayed; (b) Admin edit-user modal saves first_name change with 200 response and 'User updated successfully' toast — 'Failed to update user' error no longer occurs.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:327-332 (user_to_public) — sanitizer only handles '' -> None. Consider also handling non-int strings like '0' safely; currently Pydantic Optional[int] coerces '0' fine but any non-numeric string would still 500. Low risk since agent-create-user is the only source and it now writes None.

server.py:330 — condition `if user.get('timer_duration_hours') == '' or user.get('timer_duration_hours') == '':` has a duplicated clause (same string twice). Harmless but should be simplified to a single `== ''` check.

server.py:651 (agent_my_clients) — `u.get('timer_duration_hours') or None` correctly maps '' and 0 to None. Note: this ALSO coerces a legitimate 0-hour timer to None, which is likely intended (0h = disabled) but worth an inline comment.
server.py:2344-2345 (admin_update_user) — same falsy check pattern applied consistently. Good.
Bot-detection middleware still requires browser User-Agent; test suite uses one.

rca of the issue: Root cause: agent-create-user endpoint stored `timer_duration_hours` field as empty string '' when the agent omitted it. UserPublic Pydantic model declares it as Optional[int]. When admin update endpoint returned user_to_public(updated_user), Pydantic tried to coerce '' into Optional[int] and raised ValidationError -> 500 'Failed to update user'. Login was similarly failing whenever the model was serialized. Fix: (a) server.py:329-331 user_to_public() sanitizes '' -> None before Pydantic parse; (b) server.py:651 agent_my_clients uses `or None` to normalize; (c) admin_update_user (server.py:2344-2345) sets None when falsy; (d) existing DB records with '' were migrated to null (verified: mongosh count of {timer_duration_hours:''} = 0). Reproduction: prior to the fix, POST /api/public/agent-create-user without timer_duration_hours -> user row had timer_duration_hours:''. Then POST /api/auth/login as that user or PUT /api/admin/users/{id} would return 500. Mitigation verified: all 5 pytest cases pass and UI edit succeeds with 200.
